items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: even more so, like Benny Pollock and our Goldkette band

ctx.x: And -- but that sort of thing gives us a little bit of Americana, a little bit of mystery in the early jazz period. And it was the Jazz Age. I always tie in the swing age up to Benny Goodman when he made his famous trip across the country, when he got out to California, and besides I've divided almost, although this isn't quite accurate, but generally speaking, we delved into two beat music. We didn't have the influence of the Latins, of the Latin people coming up here and giving this eight / eight in and a bar.…
even more so, like Benny Pollock and our Goldkette band, and even you know the Whiteman band was like that for a time in the early '30s or late 1920s, when we were developing a lot.

But then you have to have -- the people have to buy it, and they stopped buying that. They were ready for something else, and they got it out of radio. So I'm not -- I can't deny that eight in and a bar -- did a lot of it with Shaw, did a lot of it with the Glen Gray band, that is, not to get mixed up with the early Casa Loma. That was when all these guys used percussive sounds, particularly in the bass. Everything had to be four beats.
